ai.description: This slender colubrid reaches 1.5m. It is pale yellow or tan with dark, diamond-shaped dorsal blotches and a distinctive dark "diadem" marking across the head. A dark stripe extends from each eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Spalerosophis atriceps* by the presence of a distinct, dark "diadem" or V-shaped marking on the crown, which is absent in similar-looking rat snakes or racers.
ai.habitat: The Diadem Snake inhabits arid and semi-arid regions, including sandy deserts, scrublands, and rocky foothills, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Diadem Snake is primarily diurnal and actively hunts by patrolling rocky crevices and burrows to flush out small mammals and lizards.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Spalerosophis atriceps* is oviparous, typically breeding in spring and laying a clutch of 5–15 eggs that hatch after an incubation period of roughly two months.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Spalerosophis atriceps* occurs across northern and western India, ranging from the arid plains of Rajasthan to the Himalayan foothills up to 2,000 meters.
